verses.text: After these things, while Artaxerxes was king of Persia, there was a man named Ezra. He was the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest.

This Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a teacher who knew the law of Moses very well, the law the LORD, the God of Israel, had given. The king gave him everything he asked for, because the LORD his God was helping him.
Some of the Israelites went up to Jerusalem with him in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes. With them were some priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants.
Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the king's seventh year.
He had left Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, because his God's kind hand was on him.
Ezra had set his heart on studying the LORD's law, obeying it, and teaching its rules and decisions in Israel.
This is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and teacher, who studied the LORD's commands and rules for Israel:
"From Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, teacher of the law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
I order that any of the people of Israel in my kingdom, including their priests and Levites, who want to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
You are being sent by the king and his seven advisers to check on how well Judah and Jerusalem are obeying the law of your God, which you have with you.
Take with you the silver and gold that the king and his advisers have freely given to the God of Israel, whose home is in Jerusalem.
Also take all the silver and gold you receive from the province of Babylon, along with the gifts the people and priests freely give for the temple of their God in Jerusalem.
Use this money carefully to buy bulls, rams, and lambs, with their grain offerings and drink offerings. Offer them on the altar of the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
You and your fellow Jews may do whatever seems best with the rest of the silver and gold, as your God wants.
Give to the God of Jerusalem all the things that have been given to you for the service in the temple of your God.
If you need anything else for the temple of your God, you may pay for it from the king's treasury.
I, King Artaxerxes, order all the treasurers west of the Euphrates River to give Ezra the priest, teacher of the law of the God of heaven, whatever he asks of you, with all care,
up to about three and a half tonnes of silver, one hundred loads of wheat, about two thousand liters of wine, about two thousand liters of olive oil, and as much salt as he needs.
Whatever the God of heaven commands for his temple must be done fully and carefully. Why should his anger come on the kingdom of the king and his sons?
We also tell you that you must not make any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or other workers at this temple of God pay any taxes, payments, or fees.
And you, Ezra, use the wisdom your God has given you to choose judges and leaders to judge all the people west of the Euphrates River who know the laws of your God. Teach those who do not know them.
Anyone who does not obey the law of your God and the law of the king must be punished quickly, by death, by being sent away, by having their property taken, or by prison."
Ezra said: Praise the LORD, the God of our ancestors, who put it into the king's heart to make the LORD's temple in Jerusalem beautiful.

He has shown me his faithful love in front of the king, his advisers, and all his powerful officials. Because the LORD my God was helping me, I had courage, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
